precepts.text: In those days there was no king in Israel; every man did that which was right in his own eyes, and that includes taking heathen women.
precepts.point: Ruth clave to Naomi: thy people shall be my people and thy God my God; she is the picture of the ten men who will take hold of the skirt of a Jew and say, we will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Naomi told Ruth, “Behold, thy sister in law is gone back unto her people, and unto her gods”. Orpah went back to Moab, to her people and her gods. These were not Israelite women; this was a heathen woman of another nation. That is important, because there are doctrines out there teaching that Ruth was an Israelite. No, she was not. She was a heathen. Was it right for Boaz to deal with a heathen? No, but it happened.

Just in case there is any confusion, the last verse of Judges, right above Ruth, shows why it happened: “In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.” During the judges, we did what we wanted to do.

And Ruth opens in that very time: “Now it came to pass in the days when the judges ruled”. There was no king. It was the time when Israel did what they wanted, and that included taking heathen women.

So Ruth's story does not make her an Israelite, and it does not make it right to take a heathen wife. It shows what Israel was doing when every man did what was right in his own eyes. The scripture keeps calling her what she is: “Ruth the Moabitess”. That is clear.

precepts.text: Ten men out of all languages of the nations shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying we will go with you; the nations will cleave to Israel in the kingdom as Ruth cleaved to Naomi.
precepts.point: Ruth clave to Naomi: thy people shall be my people and thy God my God; she is the picture of the ten men who will take hold of the skirt of a Jew and say, we will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Ruth said, “thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God”. She is a heathen saying, if I go with you, I will be as if I am an Israelite, and I will serve your God too. She is cleaving to an Israelite woman, that's all; there were no promises made to her. “Where thou diest, will I die, and there will I be buried”: I'm not leaving you.

The nations are going to be the same way in the kingdom. Zechariah shows it: “Thus saith the Lord of hosts; In those days it shall come to pass, that ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you.”

We will go with you, just like Ruth said. For we have heard that God is with you: your God is a real God, and ours is garbage. They are going to cleave to Israel the way Ruth cleaved to Naomi, and they will cleave as servants.

So Ruth is the picture of the nations in the kingdom: not Israelites, but holding on to Israel because the God of Israel is the true God.

precepts.point: Were the sons of Israel supposed to take wives of the women of Moab while sojourning there? No; but remember what was just read at the end of Judges, that every man did that which was right in his own eyes. And this was not the first time Israel dealt with the women of Moab.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
The law was plain. “An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord; even to their tenth generation shall they not enter into the congregation of the Lord for ever”.

Israel was not supposed to be marrying the women of Moab. The sons of Elimelech did it anyway, because in those days every man did that which was right in his own eyes.

precepts.text: Israel had already committed whoredom with the daughters of Moab at Shittim, and the people did eat and bowed down to their gods.
precepts.point: Were the sons of Israel supposed to take wives of the women of Moab while sojourning there? No; but remember what was just read at the end of Judges, that every man did that which was right in his own eyes. And this was not the first time Israel dealt with the women of Moab.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
This was not the first time Israel dealt with the women of Moab. “And Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab. And they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods: and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods.”

At Shittim the daughters of Moab drew Israel into whoredom, and from there into the sacrifices of their gods, eating and bowing down to them. That is the history behind the law, and it is what Israel was stepping back into when the sons of Naomi took wives of Moab.

precepts.text: Even in the time of Ezra, Israel had not put away the strange people of the land, the Moabites among them; remember that it says the strange people of the land.
precepts.point: Were the sons of Israel supposed to take wives of the women of Moab while sojourning there? No; but remember what was just read at the end of Judges, that every man did that which was right in his own eyes. And this was not the first time Israel dealt with the women of Moab.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
Israel kept dealing with the women of Moab long after this. Even in the time of Ezra: “The nation of Israel, the princes, the priests and Levites, have not put away from them the strange people of the land, nor the pollutions of the Gentiles to wit, of the Canaanites, Hittites, Pheresites, Jebusites, and the Moabites, Egyptians, and Edomites.”

The Moabites are named among the strange people of the land, and remember that it says the strange people of the land. Orpah and Ruth were of those strange people, and the sons of Israel took them to wife when the law said a Moabite should not enter into the congregation.

precepts.text: A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children's children.
precepts.point: The Lord grant you that ye may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband: that rest is an inheritance. The man is supposed to leave an inheritance; you are not supposed to leave your wife and your children desolate with a gang of bills. To leave an inheritance you first have to work, and you have to be wise with how you deal with your money.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
Naomi prays that her daughters in law may find rest, each in the house of her husband. That rest is an inheritance, and it is what a man is supposed to leave behind. “A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children’s children: and the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the just.”

A good man does not leave his wife and children desolate with a gang of bills; he leaves something to his children's children. Building our legacy and passing it down is one of the things we lack in Israel today, and it is important that we get back to it.

precepts.text: Providing for your own house is where leaving an inheritance begins; first you have to work.
precepts.point: The Lord grant you that ye may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband: that rest is an inheritance. The man is supposed to leave an inheritance; you are not supposed to leave your wife and your children desolate with a gang of bills. To leave an inheritance you first have to work, and you have to be wise with how you deal with your money.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
Leaving an inheritance begins with providing for your own house. “But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.”

To leave an inheritance you first have to work, and you have to be wise with how you deal with your money. Some of us use captivity as an excuse not to better ourselves or build, but that is not what the scriptures say: get the job, further your education, do more for yourself, your family and the body. A man who does not provide for his own has denied the faith.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
Reading ahead for understanding: “What day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance.”

Behind the words the wife of the dead stands the law of the husband's brother. Whoever bought the field of Naomi had to take Ruth, the wife of the dead, with it, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance. That is the rest in the house of her husband that Naomi wished for her daughters in law: an inheritance, and a name kept in the earth.

precepts.text: The example of a widow finding rest in the house of her husband: Manasses left Judith gold, silver, servants, cattle, and lands, and she remained upon them.
precepts.point: The Lord grant you that ye may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband: that rest is an inheritance. The man is supposed to leave an inheritance; you are not supposed to leave your wife and your children desolate with a gang of bills. To leave an inheritance you first have to work, and you have to be wise with how you deal with your money.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
Judith is the example of a widow finding rest in the house of her husband. “So Judith was a widow in her house three years and four months.” She made her a tent upon the top of her house, put on sackcloth and her widow's apparel, and “fasted all the days of her widowhood”, except the eves of the sabbaths and the sabbaths, the new moons, and the feasts and solemn days of the house of Israel.

“She was also of a goodly countenance, and very beautiful to behold: and her husband Manasses had left her gold, and silver, and menservants and maidservants, and cattle, and lands; and she remained upon them.” Manasses left an inheritance, and Judith remained upon it. That is what the rest Naomi spoke of looks like: a husband who worked and left his wife provided for, not desolate.

precepts.text: The wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger; her husband's brother shall take her to wife, and the firstborn shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead.
precepts.point: Behind the words the wife of the dead stands the law of the husband's brother: if brethren dwell together and one dies having no child, his brother takes the widow to wife, and the firstborn she bears succeeds in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. That first child is basically the dead brother's child; he gets the rights of inheritance as if the brother were still alive, so the brother's name stays in the earth and his house is built up.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
The law of the husband's brother stands behind the wife of the dead. “If brethren dwell together, and one of them die, and have no child, the wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger: her husband’s brother shall go in unto her, and take her to him to wife, and perform the duty of an husband’s brother unto her.”

“And it shall be, that the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead, that his name be not put out of Israel.” That first child is basically the dead brother's child. He gets the rights of inheritance as if the brother were still alive, so the brother's name stays in the earth and his house is built up.

We are not under that law anymore; we do not have that land inheritance in captivity. It is wicked to pull that scripture today to try to get with your brother's wife after he passes away. Do not be looking at your brother's wife.

precepts.text: If the man refused, the widow loosed his shoe and spat in his face before the elders, because he would not build up his brother's house; keeping the name going was the whole purpose of the law.
precepts.point: Behind the words the wife of the dead stands the law of the husband's brother: if brethren dwell together and one dies having no child, his brother takes the widow to wife, and the firstborn she bears succeeds in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. That first child is basically the dead brother's child; he gets the rights of inheritance as if the brother were still alive, so the brother's name stays in the earth and his house is built up.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
If the brother refused his duty, the law shamed him for it. “And if the man like not to take his brother’s wife, then let his brother’s wife go up to the gate unto the elders, and say, My husband’s brother refuseth to raise up unto his brother a name in Israel, he will not perform the duty of my husband’s brother.”

The elders would call him and speak to him, and if he stood to it and said “I like not to take her”, then his brother's wife would come to him before the elders, “and loose his shoe from off his foot, and spit in his face, and shall answer and say, So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother’s house. And his name shall be called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.”

Keeping the name going was the whole purpose of the law. A man who would not build up his brother's house carried that shame on his own name in Israel.

That is why the law had the firstborn of the widow succeed in the name of the dead brother. You want somebody to carry on your name; the firstborn carries the weight of it.

precepts.text: Reuben was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph; the birthright shows why the firstborn and the inheritance mattered so much in Israel.
precepts.point: Behind the words the wife of the dead stands the law of the husband's brother: if brethren dwell together and one dies having no child, his brother takes the widow to wife, and the firstborn she bears succeeds in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
“Now the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel, (for he was the firstborn; but, forasmuch as he defiled his father’s bed, his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph the son of Israel: and the genealogy is not to be reckoned after the birthright.”

Reuben was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph. The birthright shows why the firstborn and the inheritance mattered so much in Israel, and why the law took such care that a dead brother's name and inheritance were raised up.

Even in the seventy years under Babylon the Lord said: “Build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them; Take ye wives, and beget sons and daughters; and take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands, that they may bear sons and daughters; that ye may be increased there, and not diminished.”

precepts.text: In Israel the younger widows are refused, for when they begin to wax wanton against Christ they will marry; a young widow still has years to bear children and that urge will most likely come upon her, which is why Naomi released them.
precepts.point: Naomi was free of her responsibility toward them: her husband had died, her sons their husbands had died, and their husbands had left them inheritances in Moab. She would not put them under an oath to stay and wait for sons that would likely never come.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
Naomi would not hold her daughters in law to wait for sons that would likely never come. In Israel the same thing is understood of young widows: “But the younger widows refuse: for when they have begun to wax wanton against Christ, they will marry”.

A young widow still has years to bear children, and that urge will most likely come upon her; she is not going to wait. Orpah and Ruth were grown women, and Naomi was free of her responsibility toward them: her husband had died, her sons their husbands had died, and their husbands had left them inheritances in Moab. So she would not put them under an oath to stay, and released them.

precepts.text: All the gods of the nations are idols, but the Lord made the heavens; what Orpah returned to were idols.
precepts.point: Naomi said, Thy sister in law is gone back unto her people and unto her gods. Those gods were idols; Chemosh was the god the Moabites served.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
Orpah went back unto her people and unto her gods. What were those gods? “For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.”

What Orpah returned to were idols. The gods of Moab were the gods of a nation, and all the gods of the nations are idols; only the Lord made the heavens.

precepts.text: Woe to thee, Moab; thou art undone, O people of Chemosh. Chemosh was the god Moab was serving.
precepts.point: Naomi said, Thy sister in law is gone back unto her people and unto her gods. Those gods were idols; Chemosh was the god the Moabites served.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
“Woe to thee, Moab! thou art undone, O people of Chemosh: he hath given his sons that escaped, and his daughters, into captivity unto Sihon king of the Amorites.”

Moab is called the people of Chemosh. Chemosh was the god the Moabites served, the idol Orpah went back to.

precepts.text: When Solomon was old his strange wives turned away his heart, and he built an high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab; the scripture shows numerous times that Chemosh was the god of the Moabites.
precepts.point: Naomi said, Thy sister in law is gone back unto her people and unto her gods. Those gods were idols; Chemosh was the god the Moabites served.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
The scripture shows numerous times that Chemosh was the god of the Moabites. “For it came to pass, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father.” Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians and Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites, and did evil in the sight of the Lord.

“Then did Solomon build an high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, in the hill that is before Jerusalem, and for Molech, the abomination of the children of Ammon.” Chemosh is the abomination of Moab. His strange wives turned Solomon's heart to it; and those same gods of Moab are what Orpah returned to when she left Naomi.

precepts.text: Christ said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel, and the woman answered, Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters' table; because she acknowledged who he is, who she is, and who the children of Israel are, he said, O woman, great is thy faith, and her daughter was made whole.
precepts.point: Does that mean she would inherit the kingdom as a Moabitess? No. She joined herself under Israel and acknowledged her place in the hierarchy under Israel, and the scriptures give examples of strangers who did the same.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
Ruth cleaved to Naomi: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God. Does that mean she would inherit the kingdom as a Moabitess? No. She joined herself under Israel and acknowledged her place in the hierarchy under Israel, and the scriptures give examples of strangers who did the same.

Christ said, “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” The woman worshipped him and said, “Lord, help me.” He answered, “It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.” And she said, “Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.”

She acknowledged who he is, who she is, and who the children of Israel are. Because of that he said, “O woman, great is thy faith: be it unto thee even as thou wilt. And her daughter was made whole from that very hour.” That is the place Ruth took: under Israel, with Israel's God as her God.

precepts.text: Rahab the harlot and her father's household were saved alive and she dwelt in Israel, because she knew the fame of what the God of Israel had done and that the hearts of her people had melted; she knew the Most High was the true living God.
precepts.point: Does that mean she would inherit the kingdom as a Moabitess? No. She joined herself under Israel and acknowledged her place in the hierarchy under Israel, and the scriptures give examples of strangers who did the same.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
Rahab is another stranger who joined herself under Israel. “And Joshua saved Rahab the harlot alive, and her father’s household, and all that she had; and she dwelleth in Israel even unto this day; because she hid the messengers, which Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.”

Rahab knew the fame of what the God of Israel had done and that the hearts of her people had melted; she knew the Most High was the true living God. So she and her father's household were saved alive, and she dwelt in Israel. Like Ruth saying thy God my God, she acknowledged Israel's God and took her place under Israel.

precepts.text: Laban said, I have learned by experience that the Lord hath blessed me for thy sake; Laban knew where his blessings came from, for he had little before Jacob arrived and increased while our forefather served him.
precepts.point: Does that mean she would inherit the kingdom as a Moabitess? No. She joined herself under Israel and acknowledged her place in the hierarchy under Israel, and the scriptures give examples of strangers who did the same.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
Laban also knew where his blessings came from. “And Laban said unto him, I pray thee, if I have found favour in thine eyes, tarry: for I have learned by experience that the Lord hath blessed me for thy sake.”

Laban had little before Jacob arrived and increased while our forefather served him, and he learned by experience that the Lord blessed him for Jacob's sake. Ruth saw the same in Naomi: whither thou goest, I will go, because the blessing is with Israel and Israel's God.

precepts.text: Naomi had asked, Would ye tarry for sons till they were grown? Boaz's words point back to this: Ruth did what no young widow was expected to do, seeking the kinsman of her dead husband instead of following young men.
precepts.point: Boaz blessed her: thou hast shewed more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning, inasmuch as thou followedst not young men, whether poor or rich. Ruth could have gone after other men, but even as a Moabitess she was following the customs of Israel, trying to find someone to raise up seed for her dead lord and keep his name in the earth; she was trying to do the right thing and keep the laws of Israel.

note.label: Ruth 3: The Skirt of the Near Kinsman

precepts.why:
Boaz's words point back to what Naomi had asked on the road out of Moab. “Turn again, my daughters, go your way; for I am too old to have an husband. If I should say, I have hope, if I should have an husband also to night, and should also bear sons; Would ye tarry for them till they were grown? would ye stay for them from having husbands?”

No young widow was expected to wait like that; Naomi released them because of it. Yet Ruth did what none expected: she followed not young men, whether poor or rich, but sought the kinsman of her dead husband. Even as a Moabitess she followed the customs of Israel, trying to raise up seed for her dead lord and keep his name in the earth. That is the kindness Boaz says she shewed more in the latter end than at the beginning: she was trying to do the right thing and keep the laws of Israel.

points: A famine in Canaan sent Elimelech, Naomi and their two sons from Bethlehem-judah to the country of Moab, the same way a famine sent Jacob's family to Egypt.
Elimelech died, the sons took Moabite wives, Orpah and Ruth, and then the sons died too, leaving Naomi with no man in the house.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: Orpah went back to her people and unto her gods; that settles it, these were heathen women, not Israelites, whatever doctrines say about Ruth.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: Ruth clave to Naomi: thy people shall be my people and thy God my God; she is the picture of the ten men who will take hold of the skirt of a Jew and say, we will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: It came to pass in the days when the judges ruled: the scripture is putting Ruth in a time frame. Ruth takes place in the same time as the book of Judges.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

points: There was a famine in the land, and Elimelech of Bethlehemjudah went to sojourn in the country of Moab with his wife Naomi and his two sons Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites of Bethlehemjudah.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

points: Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left with her two sons. The sons took them wives of the women of Moab, Orpah and Ruth, and after they dwelt there about ten years Mahlon and Chilion died also, leaving Naomi without her husband and without her sons.

Were the sons of Israel supposed to take wives of the women of Moab while sojourning there? No; but remember what was just read at the end of Judges, that every man did that which was right in his own eyes. And this was not the first time Israel dealt with the women of Moab.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

points: Naomi heard in the country of Moab that the Lord had visited his people and given them bread, so she arose with her daughters in law to return unto the land of Judah, and told them, Go, return each to her mother's house; the Lord deal kindly with you, as ye have dealt with the dead and with me.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

points: Behind the words the wife of the dead stands the law of the husband's brother: if brethren dwell together and one dies having no child, his brother takes the widow to wife, and the firstborn she bears succeeds in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. That first child is basically the dead brother's child; he gets the rights of inheritance as if the brother were still alive, so the brother's name stays in the earth and his house is built up.

We are not under that law anymore; we do not have that land inheritance in captivity. It is wicked to pull that scripture today to try to get with your brother's wife after he passes away; do not be looking at your brother's wife.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

points: The Lord grant you that ye may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband: that rest is an inheritance. The man is supposed to leave an inheritance; you are not supposed to leave your wife and your children desolate with a gang of bills. To leave an inheritance you first have to work, and you have to be wise with how you deal with your money.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

points: The daughters in law said, Surely we will return with thee unto thy people; but Naomi answered, Are there yet any more sons in my womb, that they may be your husbands? Even if she had a husband that night and bore sons, would they tarry until the boys were grown? They were grown women; they were not going to wait.

Naomi was free of her responsibility toward them: her husband had died, her sons their husbands had died, and their husbands had left them inheritances in Moab. She would not put them under an oath to stay and wait for sons that would likely never come.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

points: They lifted up their voice and wept again; Orpah kissed her mother in law and went back, but Ruth clave unto her.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

points: Naomi said, Thy sister in law is gone back unto her people and unto her gods. Those gods were idols; Chemosh was the god the Moabites served.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

points: Ruth was determined: Intreat me not to leave thee; whither thou goest, I will go; thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God; where thou diest, will I die. She was saying, do not put me away; Orpah may have gone back, but I am going to cleave unto you.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

points: When Naomi saw that Ruth was stedfastly minded to go with her, she left speaking unto her, and the two went until they came to Bethlehem, where all the city was moved about them and said, Is this Naomi?

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

points: She answered, Call me not Naomi, call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me. I went out full, and the Lord hath brought me home again empty.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

points: So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess her daughter in law with her, and they came to Bethlehem in the beginning of barley harvest.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab
